Like the title says, there very much needs to be added an option with in the account settings page that allows an individual user to specify which of the three ordering-tabs (Hot, New, or Top) is selected by default when said user visits any subverse..

Many users have a preference of sorting order for the majority of subverses that they visit (for example, I sort things by "Top" 99% of the time.. An other user on this site has stated that he uses "New" most of the time)..

I would consider this almost a mandatory option, because with out such an option, it causes a large percentage of the users to have to load one page twice.. The first time being when the page loads in the now-default "Hot"-ordering setting, and then again when that person immediately switches to the ordering setting that they really prefer..

What this means is that, if this suggestion is implemented, it could save this site an untold amount of redundant bandwidth in the long-run.. It would basically be making the site more efficient, and giving the user what they want right away.. And of course it is tedious having to always select which ordering-tab you want every time you visit a different subverse..

Actually, I am somewhat surprised that reddit has never implemented any options such as this.. It really could have saved reddit so much wasted bandwidth.. The way that the submissions are ordered really is a preference that differs with each individual, and as such, should be realized by adding an option for it in the account settings some where..
Add an option in account settings to specify which order-tab (Hot/New/Top) is defaultly selected..

I don't see how anyone can defend the idea of making large profits off of students. This is a time in people's lives when they are trying to get a start in life and during which money is usually hard to come by. From insanely expensive textbooks that mysteriously change every year to crushing student loan debt, apparently students are seen by society as little more than mobile cash machines.

You could ask highly-respected Harvard educated MIT Economist James M Poterba. He promotes ideas like this:

>Claims of the regressivity of gasoline taxes typically rely on annual surveys of consumer income and expenditures, which show that gasoline expenditures are a larger fraction of income for low-income households than for middle- or high-income households. This paper argues that annual expenditure provides a more reliable indicator of household well-being than annual income. (Italics in original, bold added)

Yes, you read that right. Let's not look at income, let's look at what is spent!

While this particular paper is about gasoline taxes, this is a common theme in his work. It applies to student loans too. Let's look at what people spend, not what they earn.
So what's the alternative? Higher education provided by our ever-benevolent government? No thank you to state-sponsored indoctrination and another step towards socialism.

There seems to be a disconnect between the truth and what these for-profit colleges tell potential students. I think that's the real problem. I'm fine with them making money, if, and only if, they are 100% honest and upfront about the product they offer. But then no one in their right mind would buy their product. It's like selling someone a fork for eating soup and claiming it's great for eating soup.
